root_idea.summary: The root centers on pouring something out or causing it to flow forth.
root_idea.development: The imagery of poured liquid extends to descriptions of continual flow, rapid movement, liveliness, and channels or things that convey water.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The sole Quran-attested group is a passive participle and is displayed under its normalized citation form.

senses.definition: Poured forth; made to flow out.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quran, used of water in the expression ماءٍ مَسْكُوبٍ, describing water poured or flowing forth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pour out or forth; to flow or become poured out.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used intransitively of water, tears, and the like, and transitively of pouring them out.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Poured-out or running water; something continually pouring or pouring abundantly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to water and, by extension, to blood, clouds, or a wound that pours; the forms may function as descriptive epithets.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Flowing or pouring, especially of tears.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The active-participle form is applied to tears; a passive-participle form مُنْسَكِبٌ is also reported for this idea.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fleet, swift, wide-stepping, or excellent in running; brisk and lively.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a horse, and also to a person or boy in the sense of being light-spirited, active, or sprightly.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thin, delicate kind of cloth or garment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative description likening the cloth's thinness to pouring water.
Reported as an application to a man and as a dialectal variant of سَقْبٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A necessary or unavoidable thing or affair; an unavoidable disgrace.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in an idiomatic or figurative expression for something that cannot be evaded, including an inescapable disgrace.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Copper or brass; also reported for lead.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The identification varies among authorities, with lead given as an alternative or additional meaning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A named plant or tree of the plains and valleys, variously identified with several fragrant or flowering plants.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported identifications include a fragrant herb or tree, a yellow-flowered plant, the anemone, and a hot-season tree.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A name given to certain horses.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The names are associated with the sense of being fleet or swift.
A traditional name for the eleventh zodiacal sign, also called الدَّلْوُ.
The word is explained through the related form أُسْكُفَّةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Lightning extending downward toward the earth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The image is understood as though the lightning were pouring forth rain.
For trees other than palms, other terms are reported instead.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A shoemaker or leather worker; also a blacksmith.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is given as equivalent to إِسْكَافٌ, with blacksmith reported as an additional sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The higher or highest small irrigation channel from which other channels receive water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A small conveying channel used to distribute irrigation water.
A doubtful manuscript reading reported in connection with the word; the source itself suspects a transcription error.

cautions: The Quranic occurrence is the passive participle مَسْكُوبٌ; related verbs, nouns, adjectives, and derived forms are therefore kept as distinct Classical Arabic entries.
The botanical identifications under سَكَبٌ and the Milky Way identification under المِسْكَبَةُ are reported with source-level variation or manuscript uncertainty.
